name: DaVinci Deliver Codec Render Queue And Archive
use_when: A Resolve timeline needs final export, web upload, client review, archive, or editing handoff settings.
The agent must choose between H.264, H.265, ProRes, DNxHR, uncompressed, single clip, or individual clips.
The project needs both compact delivery and high-quality archive variants.
avoid_when: The user supplied exact delivery specs that must be followed instead.
The timeline still has offline media, wrong range, unmixed audio, or unresolved QC failures.
The export codec is unavailable on the current Resolve edition or operating system.

timeline_pattern.pattern: choose_timeline_range -> video_tab_container_codec -> audio_tab -> file_name_location -> add_to_render_queue -> render -> watch_output
timeline_pattern.single_clip_rule: Use Single Clip for a finished movie export.
timeline_pattern.individual_clip_rule: Use Individual Clips for conversion, roundtrip, or per-shot handoff.
timeline_pattern.container_rule: Container/format is the box; codec is the compression method.
timeline_pattern.web_rule: H.264/H.265 are compact web options; test playback and platform compatibility.
timeline_pattern.archive_rule: ProRes 422 HQ or DNxHR-style mezzanine exports are better for handoff/archive than tiny web codecs.
timeline_pattern.audio_archive_rule: For archive/handoff, preserve separate timeline audio tracks when future remix or replacement is likely.

motion.rule: Render motion-heavy sections and watch the file for dropped frames, compression artifacts, or wrong range.

sound.rule: Export audio settings should match the delivery: final stereo mix for upload, separate tracks or high-quality PCM for archive/handoff.

captions.rule: Check whether captions are burned in, sidecar, or excluded based on delivery target.

color.rule: Check exported file color/gamma and compression, not only Resolve viewer appearance.

keyframe_values.youtube_upres_note: Upscaling 1080p to UHD for upload can sometimes trigger better platform compression, but test before adopting it as a default.
keyframe_values.avoid_uncompressed: Avoid uncompressed video unless a workflow explicitly requires huge files.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use explicit format/codec/audio settings such as mp4+h264/h265 for web, mov+prores/dnxhr for handoff, PCM audio for archive, and checksum/watch pass after render.
implementation.remotion: Store delivery profiles with container, codec, bitrate/quality, audio format, captions mode, output path, and archive flag.
implementation.blender: Render image sequence or mezzanine video for archive, then encode distribution copies separately.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Export separate versions for platform upload and archive when quality/handoff matters; verify final file after export.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Export/Media Encoder presets with explicit range, codec, audio tracks, filename suffix, and watchback QC.

common_mistakes: Exporting a selected range or wrong timeline by accident.
Choosing H.264/H.265 for an edit handoff that needs a higher-quality mezzanine file.
Using uncompressed video and creating impractical file sizes.
Forgetting that codec availability can vary by Resolve edition or operating system.
Adding jobs to the render queue without checking filenames, range, and destination.
Calling the project finished before watching the exported file.
qc: Does the render range/timeline match the intended final version?
Do container, codec, resolution, frame rate, audio, filename, and destination match the delivery purpose?
Is the export compact enough for upload or high-quality enough for archive/handoff as required?
Are captions included or excluded in the intended mode?
Was the final exported file watched for playback, color, audio, black frames, and wrong range?
